item.title: Senior Expert I - Corporate Risk and Benchmarking, 9.40 months, Evaluation Office, New York, REMOTELY (Open For International Candidates), Req#596756
item.description: The UNICEF Evaluation Office (EO) is commissioning a global evaluation of UNICEF’s risk governance frameworks and practices in humanitarian action. Building on a set of case studies conducted across different emergency contexts, the evaluation will allow tracing the decision-making processes that led to either action or no action during past emergency responses and will attempt to measure their repercussion on the delivery of services and good to children, especially those in hard-to-reach areas. The evaluation aims to put forward recommendations that will equip UNICEF staff across a variety of emergency contexts to manage, prevent and share risks more responsibly and effectively in the future. The EO is seeking a Corporate Risk Benchmarking Expert for this evaluation.

item.title: Supply & Logistics Specialist (Planning and Replenishment), P-3, Temporary Position, Copenhagen, 364 days, Supply Division, #00130576
item.description: The Warehouse and Inventory Management Centre (WIMC) is responsible for receiving, storing, packing and dispatching supplies at UNICEF global hubs in support of programme operations and humanitarian action as well as for inventory forecasting and planning for standard and emergency stockpiles. WIMC manages inventory levels and sales orders for standard stock materials, packing, processing and facilitating the deliveries to countries. WIMC also provides oversight and management of the UNICEF Supply and Logistics Hubs in Copenhagen, as well as in Brindisi, Dubai, and other global hubs as needed. In collaboration with the Global Transport & Logistics Centre (GTLC), WIMC also provides oversight and normative support for the management of warehouse operations in Regional and Country Offices. The Replenishment and Order Fulfillment unit (ROFU) is responsible for the effective replenishment of standard stock materials in SD managed warehouses and hubs with optimal stock levels to meet kit production and country demand as well as for the order fulfillment and processing for SD warehouse deliveries. The Replenishment Planning team in the unit manages the materials planning, authorizes stock replenishment and schedules the kit production. The Customer Service team in the unit processes the country orders from the Copenhagen warehouse and global hubs, which has a direct impact on shipping, timely delivery and (emergency) programme implementation.

item.title: National coordinator on teacher/principal appraisal in schools/preschools, Education Section, 1 year 11,6 months, Tashkent, Uzbekistan (Nationals only) Home based with travel
item.description: The Government of Uzbekistan is advancing education reforms to support competency-based education (CBE) and improve learning outcomes. Through the Smart-ED Project for Improving the Quality and Efficiency of Education Services, UNICEF, in partnership with national counterparts, is supporting efforts to strengthen systems for evaluating and developing teachers and school leaders across preschool and general secondary education, including the introduction of performance appraisal mechanisms. Uzbekistan has established professional standards, teacher attestation, and school leader certification systems, providing a strong foundation for accountability, career progression, and professional growth. As reforms continue, there is an opportunity to further strengthen these systems to better support the competencies required for effective teaching and leadership in a CBE environment. International experience shows that effective teacher quality systems combine periodic attestation with continuous performance appraisal that provides regular feedback, mentoring, and professional development opportunities. Building on ongoing reforms, this assignment will strengthen the existing teacher attestation system and develop a performance appraisal framework for teachers and school leaders aligned with professional standards, competency-based education, and the national education quality assurance framework. The assignment will also develop practical tools, guidelines, and capacity-building resources to support implementation and promote continuous professional growth, school improvement, and better learning outcomes.

item.title: Education Specialist (Learning and Skills Assessment), P-4, #00133267, Fixed Term Position, Global Programme Division - Education CoE, Nairobi
item.description: Are you passionate about shaping how learning and skills are measured to improve education systems worldwide? Join UNICEF's Global Programme Division Centre of Excellence in Nairobi and help drive evidence-based education reforms that improve learning and skills outcomes for children and adolescents. As Education Specialist (Learning and Skills Assessment), you will provide strategic technical assistance to governments, UNICEF Country and Regional Offices, and partners to strengthen national assessment systems, learning measurement, and tracer studies, with a focus on transferable, digital and green skills, and secondary education outcomes. Working at the intersection of education policy, system strengthening, data, financing and innovation, you will contribute to UNICEF's Every Child Learns Education Strategy 2019-2030 and support countries in building more equitable, resilient and responsive education systems that prepare young people for life, work and active citizenship.

item.title: Supporter Content – Knowledge Management Intern, Division of Private Fundraising and Partnerships (PFP)
item.description:
UNICEF works in some of the world’s toughest places, to reach the world’s most disadvantaged children. To save their lives. To defend their rights. To help them fulfill their potential. Across 190 countries and territories, we work for every child, everywhere, every day, to build a better world for everyone. And we never give up.
UNICEF’s Division of Private Fundraising and Partnerships (PFP) has ambitious goals to deliver on income and influence. Donor engagement is an important driver of income. The Supporter Content team delivers content from emergency responses, donor stewardship content and virtual & immersive experiences (live, interactive, and compelling, where we use digital technologies to bring to life the work UNICEF is doing in emergency and non-emergency contexts). To support national committees and fundraisersthere are internal SharePoint sites for emergency fundraising support, High Value Stewardship services and a VIRTUAL and Immersive experiences ‘hub’ for fundraisers to preview, and self-serve, everything from invitations to global events, to films and VR experiences to tips and tricks guidance for staging their own Virtual and Immersive experiences. Linked to these is UNICEF’s Data Asset Management system called WeShare which houses and makes available all the content for usersto access and use in their fundraising efforts.

item.title: Project Officer (Data Platform Owner), P-2, Temporary Position, 5 months, Supply Division, Copenhagen, Denmark, #00138951
item.description: UNICEF Supply Division (SD) works to ensure equitable and inclusive access to essential supplies and services for children and their families, in development, humanitarian and fragile contexts. These supplies are critical to saving lives, supporting children’s health and education, and protecting them from abuse, exploitation, and neglect. As the UN’s largest end to end supply chain entity, UNICEF leverages its global reach, market influence, supply chain expertise and partnerships with governments, civil society, private sector, industry, and other stakeholders to meet children’s needs and protect their rights around the world. SD focuses on three result areas to maximize impact, scale, and effectiveness: strategic procurement; supply preparedness and response in humanitarian and fragile contexts; and supply chain optimization. To facilitate and accelerate progress toward these results, SD employs three change strategies: financing for supply and services, supply chain digitalization and supply chain localization.

You will lead global efforts across sanitation, WASH in Schools, and Menstrual Health and Hygiene, while supporting climate resilience, governance reforms, digital solutions, and resource mobilization. Working with partners across development and humanitarian settings, you will help shape policies, strengthen institutions, mobilize investments, and scale sustainable solutions that improve outcomes for the most vulnerable children and families.
